headline: A paper argues that latent monitors must separate prompt-injection exposure from unsafe-action commitment
summary: A paper reports that latent monitors trained on a mixed unsafe-versus-rest contrast can flag prompt-injection exposure without reliably predicting which exposed agent will take an unsafe tool action. In a generated-action AgentDojo grid, Qwen's naive contrast gives pre-action AUROC 0.556 for NLA text and 0.672 for an activation probe; training on exposed cases only raises the activation probe to 0.853, close to a matched visible-text TF-IDF baseline at 0.855. The paper reports related commitment-contrast results on Mistral-7B and OLMo-2-7B, but all three model families use AgentDojo and the generated-action study is not a live rollout.
